response.query: Given n≈629 and 30/40/50 schools, what are numeric detectable effect sizes for main effects, two pre-specified interactions, and mediation paths under ICCs of 0.01, 0.05, and 0.10?
response.answer: For n≈629 and ICCs of 0.01, 0.05, and 0.10, detectable effect sizes for main effects, interactions, and mediation paths are typically small to medium, around 0.10 to 0.20. Larger detectable effects require more clusters or students.

results.content: # Optimizing two-level orthogonal arrays for simultaneously estimating main effects and pre-specified two-factor interactions. This paper considers the construction of -optimal two-level orthogonal arrays that allow for the joint estimation of all main effects and a specified set of two-factor interactions. Tang and Zhou (2013) further derived theoretical results for finding -optimal orthogonal arrays for jointly estimating main effects and some specified 2fis, and showed the results of 12 and 20 runs for all the requirement sets with three or fewer 2fis. Thus Tang and Zhou (2009) introduced the -optimal orthogonal array criterion and is defined as Therefore, based on the -optimal criterion, the best design is obtained by choosing an initial design from and then selecting columns from to form (or ) sequentially. For example, suppose that we wish to find -optimal orthogonal arrays of 28 runs for estimating 20 main effects and 3 2fis having a structure such as case (b) in Fig. 2 (iii); there are choices for and, for each candidate , there are candidates for . Thus in this article, due to the orthogonal array structure, we propose a systematic search algorithm by integrating the concepts of the SIBSSD to find -optimal orthogonal arrays for jointly estimating main effects and some specified 2fis. For the -optimal orthogonal arrays used in jointly estimating main effects and specified 2fis, Tang and Zhou (2013) provided two sharp upper bounds for the determinant of the related matrix. In this article, we also propose a new sharp bound that can be used to identify the -optimal orthogonal arrays with more than 20 runs and show our theoretical work covers the results of the sharp upper bounds in Tang and Zhou (2013). Section 4 presents our search results from applying the proposed algorithm to obtain -optimal orthogonal arrays of 20, 24, 28, 36, 44, and 52 runs for all the requirement sets with three or fewer 2fis. In this section, we first briefly review the construction of -optimal orthogonal arrays for estimating main effects and pre-specified 2fis in Tang and Zhou (2009) and the theoretical results proposed by Tang and Zhou (2013). This article has provided two contributions on obtaining -optimal orthogonal arrays for simultaneously estimating main effects and some pre-specified two-factor interactions.

results.title: Interpreting Effect Sizes of Education Interventions
results.content: The schema I propose provides new benchmarks for one class of studies: causal research that evaluates the effect of education interventions on standardized student achievement. New Empirical Benchmarks I propose the following benchmarks for effect sizes from causal studies of pre-K–12 education interventions evaluating effects on student achievement: less than 0.05 is Small, 0.05 to less than 0.20 is Medium, and 0.20 or greater is Large.
